title: The Armor That Walks
text: A suit of black plate stands in the barrow's mouth, dented by blows that killed whoever wore it last. As you come close it turns its empty helm, slowly, toward the one of you who has killed the least. Then it opens its arms, the way a mother does.

options.label: Let the gentlest of you step into its waiting arms, trusting that it means no harm.

outcomes.text: The plates close over them one by one. When the helm shuts, the eyes inside are not quite theirs any more, and they never will be again.
It is only armor after all: very old, very good, and it fits as if it was forged for them. Perhaps it was.
It was not empty. It never was.

options.label: The strongest breaks it apart before it can move again, and before anyone is tempted.

outcomes.text: It comes apart like a dropped pot, and something sighs out of the pieces, grateful or relieved.
It does not want to be broken, and it has had a long time to learn how to fight.

options.label: Back away and go around it. Whatever wore that armor last did not walk away.

outcomes.text: It watches you go. That night it is standing at the edge of the firelight, helm turned toward the camp, and nobody sleeps well.
It watches you go, and then it is not where you left it. You hear plate on stone behind you for the rest of the day.
